title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 99
paragraphs: After Leotychides had made this suggestion, the Greeks next brought their ships up to land and disembarked on the shore. They were ranging themselves for battle; and the Persians, seeing the Greeks preparing for battle and that they had exhorted the Ionians, first deprived the Samians of their arms, suspecting they inclined to the Greek side — for when Athenian prisoners whom Xerxes's army had found left behind in Attica had come in the barbarians' ships, the Samians had ransomed them and sent them back to Athens, supplying them with means for the journey; this is why they were especially suspected, since they had ransomed five hundred of Xerxes's enemies. Secondly, the Persians appointed the Milesians to guard the passes leading to the heights of Mycale, on the pretext that they knew the country best; but the real reason was to get them out of the camp. Against these Ionians, whom they suspected would make some hostile move if they found the chance, the Persians sought to secure themselves in the manner mentioned; and they themselves then brought together their wicker shields to serve as a fence.
